titles.title: a round 1 call invokes hooks.ground once with the complete targets and no prior-findings argument
a round 2 (Correction-and-Re-review) call invokes hooks.ground through the identical call shape as round 1, differing only in the round number passed
hooks.ground receives the full targets/artifact unmodified -- nothing is stripped or withheld before grounding runs
round 0 is rejected with a RangeError before any hook is called
a negative round is rejected with a RangeError before any hook is called
a non-integer round is rejected with a RangeError before any hook is called
a rejecting hooks.ground propagates its rejection and hooks.security is never called for that round
a rejecting hooks.security propagates its rejection rather than returning hooks.ground's findings alone
an empty ReviewTargets.entries array is passed through to hooks.ground unchanged, with no special-casing
opts omitted defaults runSecurityPass to true -- hooks.security runs when it is supplied
opts.runSecurityPass:false suppresses hooks.security even when it is supplied
hooks.security undefined is a no-op, not a thrown error, when runSecurityPass is true or omitted
a large round number (e.g. 50) runs through the identical code path as round 1, with no round-number-based branching

reviewId never appears in hooks.ground's or hooks.security's own call arguments across round 1 and round 2, and is left available unchanged for the caller to thread on to the sc4/sc5 calls, never substituted for a different value
hooks.security is invoked with hooks as its receiver, so a method implementation that reads `this` does not throw
